chunks: Ali ibn Isa al-Mujawar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Muqri, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Thuwayr ibn Said, from his father Said ibn Alaqa, from al-Hasan al-Basri. He said:

The Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), ascended the pulpit of Basra and said: O people, tell me my lineage! Whoever recognizes me, let him tell my lineage. If not, then I shall tell my own lineage. I am Zayd ibn Abd Manaf ibn Amir ibn Amr ibn al-Mughira ibn Zayd ibn Kilab.
Then Ibn al-Kawwa stood up to him and said: O you! We do not know any lineage for you other than that you are Ali ibn Abi Talib ibn Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim ibn Abd Manaf ibn Qusay ibn Kilab.

So he said to him: O fool! Indeed, my father named me Zayd after his grandfather Qusay. And the name of my father is Abd Manaf, but the kunya overcame the name. And the name of Abd al-Muttalib is Amir, but the title overcame the name. And the name of Hashim is Amr, but the epithet overcame the name. And the name of Abd Manaf is al-Mughira, but the title overcame the name. And the name of Qusay is Zayd, but the Arabs called him Mujammi (the gatherer) because he gathered them from the furthest land to Mecca, so the title overcame the name.

key_terms.كنية: Kunya - an Arabic agnomen, typically of the form Abu/Umm + name
key_terms.لقب: Laqab - a title or epithet more famous than the birth name
key_terms.مجمع: Mujammi - the gatherer; title given to Qusay for uniting the Quraysh in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the real names of his ancestors on the pulpit of Basra?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Amali of al-Saduq, Imam Ali (AS) ascended the pulpit of Basra and challenged the people to state his genealogy. When Ibn al-Kawwa objected, knowing only the conventional names, Imam Ali revealed the original birth names of each ancestor, explaining how their well-known titles (kunya, laqab) had overshadowed their real names. This was a demonstration of his deep knowledge of his own lineage and Arab genealogical tradition.

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. `Isa al-Mujawar (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Muhammad b. Bandar narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. `Ali al-Muqri from Muhammad b. Sinan from Malik b. `Atiyya from Thuwayr b. Sa`id from his father Sa`id b. `Alaqa from al-Hasan al-Basri. He said:

Amir al-Mu’minin (as) climbed the pulpit of Basra and said: O people! Tell me about my lineage, for whoever recognizes me should tell me about my lineage. If not, then I will speak about my own lineage. I am Zayd b. `Abd Manaf b. `Amer b. `Amr b. al-Mughira b. Zayd b. Kilab.
So, Ibn al-Kawa’ stood and said to him: O you! We do not know of a lineage for you other than that you are `Ali b. Abi Talib b. `Abd al-Muttalib b. Hashim b. `Abd Manaf b. Qusay b. Kilab.

So, he said to him: O Laka`! Surely, my father named me Zayd after his grandfather Qusay. The name of my father is `Abd Manaf, but the agnomen (kunya) overcame the name [in popularity]. The name of `Abd al-Muttalib is `Amer, but the agnomen overcame the name. The name of Hashim is `Amr, but the agnomen overcame the name. The name of `Abd Manaf is al-Mughira, but the agnomen overcame the name. The name of Qusay is Zayd, but the Arabs called him by a merged name because he gathered them from the furthest land (al-balad al-aqsa) to Mecca, so the agnomen overcame the name.
